intro: Google has released a whole set of AI tools for building, and most people have never heard of them. Here's what each one is for and which one a business owner should open first. Check each tool's current free limits before you rely on it; Google changes them often.

free.title: Google AI Studio: build an app from a sentence
free.body:
At aistudio.google.com you can describe an app and get a working version you can try in the browser.

Copy this inBuild a simple web app for my business: [e.g. a booking request form that emails me]. Keep it to one page, mobile friendly, and explain how to put it on my website.

free.title: Stitch: design app screens
free.body: Describe the screens you want and get UI designs you can export to code or Figma. Good for showing a developer exactly what you mean.

free.title: Coding agents: Antigravity and Jules
free.body: Google's coding agents can work across a whole codebase: add features, fix bugs and explain code. Use them like Claude Code: describe the change in plain English and review what they do before you accept it.

free.title: Images and video
free.body: Google's image model (often called Nano Banana) edits and creates images from a description; Veo makes short video clips. Both are inside the Gemini app and AI Studio.

free.title: Which one to use when
free.body:
• You want a quick tool for your team: AI Studio.
  • You want to show a developer a design: Stitch.
  • You already have code to change: a coding agent.
  • You need visuals for posts: the image and video models.

Tool names, prices and limits change often. Check each tool's own page.
